- Does the platform offer region pinning/geo-fencing per-tenant?

Hi Olivia — thanks for sending this over. I'm copying Kimberly (product security) and Priya (privacy ops) for technical detail and evidence. Below are concise answers to each question; Kimberly will follow up with a deeper technical note and artifacts you can reference.

1) Where request data lives at rest (region, cloud provider):
- Hosted endpoints are provisioned in the cloud region you select at project creation (AWS, GCP, or Azure). For NovaPayment we've verified the "us-west-2" region is available. Data at rest is stored in the same region by default; control plane metadata is global but contains no customer plaintext.

2) Default retention period for inputs and generated content: 
- Default retention for request payloads and generated responses is 30 days. This default reflects production caching and short-term debug retention.

3) Delete handling and purge timelines:
- Delete flow: a) Deletion request marks records as eligible for purge; b) Background job removes from primary DB and invalidates caches; c) Objects are scheduled for S3 lifecycle deletion.
- Typical purge timelines: hot-store removal within 0–24 hours of request, object-level purge from backups within 30–90 days depending on backup window.

4) Region pinning / geo-fencing: 
- We support per-tenant region pinning for hosted endpoints (paid tier). Requests can be routed and stored only in selected region(s); cross-region failover is opt-in and documented.

5) Legal holds / eDiscovery:
- Legal holds pause deletion for specified tenant objects; requests are tracked in our ticketing system and flagged in the retention pipeline. We provide export and frozen-snapshot options for discovery.

6) Evidence:
- We can supply architecture diagrams, retention schedule docs and redacted audit logs. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited (scope details available on request).

Next steps: Kimberly will attach the technical note and a short evidence bundle (diagram + retention schedule PDF). Please tell us if you need more granularity (e.g., backup provider names, encryption key rotation schedule) and we'll add it.

Thanks,

Hi Olivia — Kimberly here from Product Security. Sorry for the short delay; below are precise answers to your clarifying questions and links to the evidence bundle. I've attached the internal retention schedule PDF and a diagram of the hosted endpoint architecture.

Q: Does "hot-store removal" include prefix/KV caches and transient model caches?
A: Yes. We operate three categories of short-term stores: (1) primary customer DB rows (metadata + pointers), (2) KV/prefix caches used for inference performance, and (3) ephemeral model attention/KV caches. Deletion request triggers an orchestration that:
- Invalidate and evict items from active KV/prefix caches immediately (sub-second to minutes) where feasible;
- Mark primary DB rows as deleted and remove them via background worker (0–24 hrs);
- Signal inference nodes to clear ephemeral KV caches for the affected tenant (clears on next process/epoch).

Q: Are snapshots immutable and is snapshot retention per-tenant?
A: Snapshots (daily) are immutable once created. Retention is managed at the tenant level in our retention service: default snapshot retention is 90 days. Customers can request shorter retention in their contract. Backups are encrypted; snapshot deletion follows a lifecycle policy that respects legal hold flags.

Q: Region pinning — automated verification to prevent accidental writes?
A: Yes. Region pinning enforces network and control-plane constraints: storage buckets and database clusters for pinned tenants are scoped to the selected region(s). Our request router carries a tenant-region claim; writes with mismatched claims are rejected and logged. We additionally run periodic compliance checks that scan recent writes and raise automated alerts if a tenant's data is found outside allowed regions.

Q: Customer-managed keys (CMK) support?
A: We support AWS KMS CMKs for hosted deployments on the Dedicated/Enterprise plans. For standard hosted API customers we use provider-managed KMS keys (with documented rotation). CMK support is available as an opt-in contract feature; Priya is copied to coordinate onboarding details.

Evidence bundle (attached / links):
- Attachment: data-lifecycle-schedule.pdf — retention timelines, snapshot policy, legal hold flow.
- Attachment: redwood-hostedapi-arch-diagram.png — region pinning and routing logic.
- Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/NovaPayment/data-lifecycle-evidence (contains SOC2 redacted summary, audit logs extract).

Operational notes:
- Erasure API: We provide a Delete / Erasure API that opens a ticket in our privacy ops queue. Tickets have SLA: initial acknowledgement in 24 hours; confirmation of hot-store purge within 72 hours; final confirmation after backup/snapshot purge per agreed retention window.
- Legal holds: flagged holds override lifecycle rules until a formal release is provided; holds are surfaced in the same ticket.
- Auditability: deletion events generate audit records (actor, request id, timestamps) retained per contract; we can provide event extracts for your audit team.

Please let us know if you'd like a small runbook we can hand to your audit team for how to verify erasure status; we can produce CSV extracts and a short verification checklist.

Regards,
